title: Baryo vs Barangay: what's the difference?
big_number_label: the year every barrio became a barangay (Presidential Decree No. 557)
takeaways: Baryo and barangay are the same thing. The barangay was the original Filipino community, led by a datu, and its name comes from the balangay, an ancient boat.
Under Spain it was called barrio, the Spanish word for neighborhood. Baryo was still the official name even in the Barrio Charter Act of 1959.
On September 21, 1974, every barrio became a barangay under PD 557. Today there are more than 42,000 barangays, the smallest unit of government.

quiz.q: Where does the word 'barangay' come from?
In what year did every barrio become a barangay?

paragraphs: This is a baryo. And this is a barangay. So what's the difference? Your lolo and lola call it baryo. But your ID says barangay. Are they really different? The answer: they're the same! So why two names? Let's go back in history.

Even before the Spaniards arrived, we already had communities called barangays. Each was led by a datu and usually had thirty to a hundred families. And the name? It comes from the balangay, the boat our ancestors used to sail. In Butuan, a balangay was dug up that is estimated to date back to the year 320!

And did you know? When the Spaniards arrived, they grouped the barangays into towns, or pueblos. And the barangays, they called barrios. Barrio is a Spanish word meaning neighborhood. In our spelling: baryo. So for a long time, baryo was what we called it. Even in 1959, when the Barrio Charter Act was passed, baryo was still the official name.

And here's more! In 1974, President Ferdinand Marcos signed Presidential Decree 557. Every barrio in the country became a barangay! Why? According to the decree itself, the word barrio is of foreign origin. So we brought back our own: barangay. Today there are more than 42,000 barangays across the Philippines. It is the smallest unit of our government.

So what's the difference? Barangay is the original and official name. Baryo comes from Spanish and is just an old name now. But when lolo says he's from the baryo, he's still right! How about you, do you call your place baryo or barangay? Comment below! And if you want more differences like this, follow Juan Fact a Day!
